questions.explanation: Rules and laws use 'have to' or 'must'.
questions.q: You ___ wear a seatbelt. It's the law.
You ___ smoke here. It's forbidden.
I ___ go now. My bus leaves in five minutes.

questions.explanation: 'Doesn't have to' means something is not necessary.
questions.q: She ___ wear glasses. Her eyes are fine.
We ___ be late for the exam.

questions.explanation: 'Don't have to' means it's not necessary.
questions.q: You ___ bring food. The restaurant serves lunch.

questions.explanation: After 'must' use the base verb, never 'to'.
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
He ___ get up early. He starts work at 6.
Students ___ cheat in exams.

questions.explanation: After 'must' use the base verb: 'must take'.
questions.q: I ___ an umbrella. It's raining. (must)
You ___ park here. You'll get a fine.

questions.explanation: 'Don't have to' means it's not necessary.
questions.q: They ___ pay. The museum is free today.

questions.explanation: With 'he' use 'doesn't have to', not 'don't have to'.
questions.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
You ___ be 18 to drive a car.
We ___ make noise. The baby is sleeping.
I ___ wear a uniform at work.
You ___ tell lies. It's wrong.
She ___ take the bus. Her car is broken.
Visitors ___ touch the paintings.

questions.explanation: No hurry = not necessary: 'don't have to'.
questions.q: You ___ hurry. We have lots of time.
